name: Paytronix
oneLiner: Guest engagement suite for restaurants and convenience stores (loyalty, online ordering, gift cards, branded apps, messaging), part of The Access Group since its acquisition announced in November 2024.
bestFor: Multi-location restaurant chains and c-store brands that want loyalty, ordering, gift cards and campaigns on one guest database.

customers.name: Las Palapas (LP Club app, 25 locations, February 2026)

updates.text: Launched Journey Builder, an AI-powered, no-code campaign automation tool for multi-step guest journeys, available to all Paytronix clients in Campaign Center.

Released Rewards Hub for loyalty customers on Access Identity, letting marketers set up rewards, change earning ratios and launch promotions themselves; tiers, clubs and point multipliers to follow later in 2026.
Brought Advanced Messaging with Journey Builder natively into Access Evo.

features: Points, visit and tiered loyalty programs with comps and promotions
Rewards Hub for self-service reward and earn-rate changes
Journey Builder AI campaign automation across email, SMS and push
Branded mobile app and online ordering
Native stored-value gift cards and e-gift cards redeemable with loyalty
POS and ordering integrations: more than 450 existing integrations, including 30+ native POS integrations (Qu, Revel and others)

pricing.text: Custom pricing; Paytronix does not publish prices. Its own comparison guide (May 2026) says 'Contact for pricing. Custom-quoted based on brand size, product modules selected, and location count.'

notes: Acquired by The Access Group (announced November 2024; https://www.restaurantdive.com/news/paytronix-acquired-by-the-access-group/731733/); keeps the Paytronix name and describes itself as 'an Access company'. Dropped from the original: the 400-500% message-effectiveness claim, 50-70% participation claim, Smashburger customer reference, and the $1,500-$5,000/month price range (unsourced). November 2026: paytronix.com/loyalty says 'more than 450 existing integrations' and that it helps restaurant groups from 1-9 units; Paytronix's May 2026 comparison guide gives '450+ integrations including 30+ native POS integrations', the pricing basis and its limitations. It also claims 1,800+ brands across 50,000 locations (vendor claim, not used). No G2 rating cited: G2's Paytronix CXP listing has only 3 reviews and G2 says that isn't enough for buying insight. Rewards Hub currently supports the Bankable Points program type only.
pros: Loyalty, online ordering, gift cards, branded apps and messaging on one guest database
Flexible programs: points, visits, tiers, subscriptions, comps and promotions
Marketers change rewards and earning ratios themselves in Rewards Hub (2026)
Journey Builder automates multi-step campaigns across email, SMS and push
More than 450 integrations, including 30+ native POS integrations

cons.text: No published prices; quotes depend on brand size, modules and location count
Paytronix's own guide says it suits operators with the budget for enterprise-tier platforms, and the smallest single-location operators may find it more extensive than needed
Rewards Hub supports only the Bankable Points program type at launch; tiers, clubs and point multipliers are due later in 2026

plans.billing: custom quote based on brand size, modules selected and location count
